title: Changing the invoice date after the customer changed term
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure Invoice A was created on Net 30, dated Oct 5, 2026 (due Nov 4, 2026); its customer has since been moved to Net 60.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open invoice A.
  2. Change its invoice date to Oct 10, 2026.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • It shows Terms Net 30, due Nov 4, 2026.

Step 2:

  • The due date becomes Nov 9, 2026 (Net 30) or Dec 9, 2026 (Net 60), as the PO answers.

S7-R7 says the invoice keeps its term; S7-R8 says a changed date is recalculated from the customer's term. Question 7 on Chris Ward's sheet (shared with him 23 Oct 2026) asks which wins; held until he answers.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R8: “When a user changes the invoice date on an invoice (existing behavior), the due date is recalculated from the customer's term by the rules above, including the shop's own terms.”
  • S7-R7: “An invoice keeps the term and due date it was created with. Changing the customer's term later, deactivating the term or moving the customer never changes an existing invoice.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
